frequency_question: What proportion of major federal partisan voting bills pass both chambers and reach enactment within a single congressional session window?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone omnibus or targeted voting reform bills with party-line divisions; excludes routine reauthorizations, non-controversial technical updates, or bills folded invisibly into must-pass appropriations without separate recorded floor votes.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act Amendments / Proof of Citizenship Proposals (REAL ID era)
Freedom to Vote Act (H.R. 1 / S. 1 equivalents)

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x); rate of 0% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of major federal electoral law pushes requiring 60 votes in the Senate.
known_gaps: Minor committee-level votes that never reached chamber floors are excluded.
skeleton: Highly polarized electoral bills introduced in divided or narrow-majority Congresses since 1994
multiplier: 0 hits out of roughly 6 major partisan attempts to pass standalone federal voter eligibility/access overhauls that cleared one chamber or saw serious floor consideration but failed filibuster thresholds or cross-party consensus.
validity_reason: Senate filibuster rules and hyper-polarized legislative dynamics remain stable through the medium term.
